courseTitle: NativeScript + Angular: Build Native iOS, Android & Web Apps

cues.en: So in this module, we added a lot of styling to the application, I showed you how to add images.
We worked on this view.
We added font icons and our own custom font to the app.
We styled different icons in the app.
And in general, you learned how styling in Natus Good works, that there are plenty of options, plenty
of different ways also for platform specific styles.
My recommended way here is the approach with different files for different platforms to have a clear
and easy to understand way of setting styles for different platforms.
And the official docs here really are your friend, especially when it comes to things like support
that CSS selectors and supported CSS as properties since these changes over time and there will be more
and more support properties as time goes by, play around with all these tools, play around with images
and get a feeling for how styling works.
Thankfully, it's relatively close to the web.
A lot of important Kazaks properties are supported and there just are some special cases like the action
bar, especially the buttons and the action bar, which are a little bit tricky to get started with.
But the main content of the page most of the time is really straightforward to set up and therefore
really fun to work with.
And now, speaking of that, now that our app has a nice, first beautiful look, let's actually proceed
with the application and let's make sure that we can do something with the user input we get here when
we try to replace or edit a challenge.
